summary: Kern County ground lookout on Piute Peak (Sequoia NF), staffed 1931-1942 per local papers; FFLOS lists it Gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Sequoia National Forest
facts.status_note: Listed Gone by the Forest Lookout Association; the sources give no year or cause for removal

visit.trail_note: Lookout Trail, 4.9 miles, from Piute Mountain Road near French Meadow to Piute Lookout Road (28S17); open to hiking, horseback riding, motorcycles and mountain biking

events.note: Theo Leibel moved to the station for the summer and took a government lookout job
Government road camp on the mountain; new road from Bodfish being built, said to make the station reachable from the Kern River side
Assistant foreman John Potter reported building a new road from Bodfish grade to the lookout station
Telephone line being put up from Tehachapi to the station
High winds made it necessary to re-anchor the lookout; Ted Leibel was stationed there
Floyd J. Walker, forest fire lookout at Piute Mountain, died when his car crashed into a ravine seven miles below the lookout

evidence.supports: Theo Leibel moved to the mountain for the summer and took the government lookout job (1931)
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Theo. Leibel have moved to Piute Mountain for the summer.

evidence.supports: Theo Leibel took the government service job as lookout (1931)
evidence.quote: Mr. Leibell has entered the government service as look-out at that station.

evidence.supports: Government road camp on the mountain and new road making the station reachable from the Kern River side (1931)
evidence.quote: This new road makes the station available from the Kern river side, shortening the auto route approximately 50 miles.

evidence.supports: Government road camp on the mountain; Caldwell employed by the forestry service on the new road from Bodfish to the station (June 25, 1931)
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Orvil Caldwell have moved for the summer to the government road camp on Piute mountain. Mr. Caldwell is employed by the forestry service in connection with the new road being built from Bodfish to the lookout station on Piute peak.

evidence.supports: Road from Bodfish to the station, being built by John Potter (1933)
evidence.quote: Assistant Foreman John Potter is building a new road from Bodfish grade to the lookout station on Piute mountain.

evidence.supports: Telephone line from Tehachapi to the station (1935)
evidence.quote: The Three C boys camped in Loraine canyon are putting up a telephone line from Tehachapi to the Piute lookout station.

evidence.supports: High winds, lookout re-anchored (June 29, 1936)
evidence.quote: The high winds sweeping over the tops of the mountains made it necessary for the lookout located on Piute to be re-anchored.

evidence.supports: Ted Leibel stationed at the lookout (1936)
evidence.quote: Ted Leibel who is located there, had several exciting moments until this was accomplished.

evidence.supports: Floyd J. Walker a forest fire lookout at Piute Mountain (1942)
evidence.quote: Floyd J. Walker, 35, 1 forest fire lookout at Piute Mountain

evidence.supports: Walker believed to have dozed at the wheel; car crashed into a shallow ravine (1942)
evidence.quote: believed to have napped at the wheel of his automobile and the car crashed into a shallow ravine

evidence.supports: Crash occurred seven miles below the lookout (1942)
evidence.quote: The accident occurred seven miles below Piute Mountain lookout

evidence.supports: Walker died in the crash (November 16, 1942)
evidence.quote: was crushed to death yesterday

evidence.supports: Walker was returning to his post after visiting family at Rosedale (1942)
evidence.quote: while Walker was enroute back to his post in the Sierra after visiting his family at Rosedale

evidence.supports: Sequoia National Forest administers the site
evidence.quote: Kern County - Sequoia National Forest

evidence.quote: Kern Piute 35.47994 -118.35937 Ground Gone

evidence.quote: The Lookout Trail is 4.9 miles long. It begins on Piute Mountain Road (28S17) near French Meadow and ends on Piute Lookout Road (28S17).

evidence.supports: Trail open to hiking, horseback riding, motorcycles and mountain biking
evidence.quote: The trail is open for the following uses: motorcycle trail riding, hiking, horseback riding, and mountain biking.

notes_for_editor: Location conflict not resolved: FFLOS gives 35.47994, -118.35937 (used in the brief); the west_us_lookouts record gives 35.45107, -118.39175. No build date or design found in the sources read. The 1931 and 1936 items spell the lookout's first name Theo and Ted; I did not assume they are the same man in the story. A trailforks listing (seen only in search results; fetch returned HTTP 403, so it is not cited) says the old Piute Lookout tower no longer exists; worth checking by hand. An undated Sequoia NF post mentions a Peak Fire near Piute Peak; not used. Budget: 2 searches, 5 page reads.
